msg: Top-level 'var' is not concurrency-safe under Swift 6 — the compiler rejects it.
fix: Make it 'let', or move it inside an actor / mark it @MainActor.

msg: 'static var' is a mutable global — the classic 'static var shared' singleton stops compiling in Swift 6 language mode.
fix: Use 'static let' for an immutable instance, or declare the type an actor / @MainActor final class.

msg: '@unchecked Sendable' silences the checker without removing the race.
fix: Keep it only next to a comment naming the lock that protects every stored property, or convert the type to an actor.

msg: 'nonisolated(unsafe)' is a migration escape hatch, not a fix — it opts the declaration out of isolation checking.
fix: Track it as debt: isolate the storage to an actor or make it immutable.

msg: '@preconcurrency import' downgrades Sendable errors from that module to warnings.
fix: Re-check this import when the dependency ships its own Sendable annotations; the shim hides real errors until then.

msg: 'DispatchQueue.main.async' inside a file that already uses async/await hops the main thread without telling the isolation checker.
fix: Use '@MainActor' on the function or 'await MainActor.run { }'.

msg: 'Task.detached' drops the enclosing actor isolation and priority, so captured state crosses an isolation boundary unchecked.
fix: Use plain 'Task { }' unless you truly need to leave the actor; then pass only Sendable values.

msg: '@escaping' closure without '@Sendable' — if it is called from another isolation domain Swift 6 rejects the call site.
fix: Write '@escaping @Sendable' or replace the completion handler with an 'async' function.

msg: DispatchSemaphore blocks a cooperative-pool thread; inside async code that can deadlock the whole pool.
fix: Await the value instead (async/await, AsyncStream, or 'withCheckedContinuation').

msg: Serial-queue '.sync { }' is the Swift 5 locking pattern; it is invisible to the Swift 6 isolation checker.
fix: Replace the queue with an actor, or use 'Mutex' / 'OSAllocatedUnfairLock' which are Sendable-aware.

msg: Package.swift is pinned to tools version 5.x, so the package never builds in Swift 6 language mode no matter how the source looks.
fix: Raise it to 'swift-tools-version: 6.0' (or set swiftLanguageMode(.v6) per target) and fix the errors that appear.
